skill.name: baseline-ui
skill.description: Enforces an opinionated UI baseline to prevent inconsistent AI-generated interfaces.
skill.summary: Applies clear frontend UI rules for accessible, consistent, and maintainable interface work.
skill.author: ibelick

security_audit.summary: All static findings are false positives caused by Markdown examples, inline package names, CSS utility names, and prose. No runtime code, shell execution, network request, system reconnaissance, data exfiltration, or prompt injection intent was found in SKILL.md.

static_findings.snippet: - `/baseline-ui`
- `/baseline-ui <file>`
- MUST use `motion/react` (formerly `framer-motion`) when JavaScript animation is required
- SHOULD use `tw-animate-css` for entrance and micro-animations in Tailwind CSS
- MUST use `cn` utility (`clsx` + `tailwind-merge`) for class logic
- MUST use accessible component primitives for anything with keyboard or focus behavior (`Base UI`,
- SHOULD prefer [`Base UI`](https://base-ui.com/react/components) for new primitives if compatible w
- MUST add an `aria-label` to icon-only buttons
- MUST use an `AlertDialog` for destructive or irreversible actions
- NEVER use `h-screen`, use `h-dvh`
- MUST respect `safe-area-inset` for fixed elements
- NEVER block paste in `input` or `textarea` elements
- MUST animate only compositor props (`transform`, `opacity`)
- NEVER animate layout properties (`width`, `height`, `top`, `left`, `margin`, `padding`)
- SHOULD avoid animating paint properties (`background`, `color`) except for small, local UI (text,
- SHOULD use `ease-out` on entrance
- NEVER exceed `200ms` for interaction feedback
- SHOULD respect `prefers-reduced-motion`
- MUST use `text-balance` for headings and `text-pretty` for body/paragraphs
- MUST use `tabular-nums` for data
- SHOULD use `truncate` or `line-clamp` for dense UI
- NEVER modify `letter-spacing` (`tracking-*`) unless explicitly requested
- MUST use a fixed `z-index` scale (no arbitrary `z-*`)
- SHOULD use `size-*` for square elements instead of `w-*` + `h-*`
- NEVER animate large `blur()` or `backdrop-filter` surfaces
- NEVER apply `will-change` outside an active animation
- NEVER use `useEffect` for anything that can be expressed as render logic
- SHOULD prefer [`Base UI`](https://base-ui.com/react/components) for new primitives if compatible w
- SHOULD avoid animating paint properties (`background`, `color`) except for small, local UI (text,
- SHOULD avoid animating large images or full-screen surfaces

content.value_statement: AI-generated interfaces can drift into inconsistent patterns, weak accessibility, and costly animation choices. This skill applies clear frontend rules for stable, accessible, and maintainable UI work.
actual_capabilities: Applies baseline UI constraints to frontend work in a conversation.
Reviews a target file and reports violations with exact snippets.
Defines stack rules for Tailwind CSS, motion/react, tw-animate-css, and cn utilities.
Sets accessibility expectations for component primitives, focus behavior, and icon-only labels.
Sets animation, typography, layout, performance, and design constraints.
limitations: Does not execute automated UI tests or inspect rendered screenshots by itself.
Does not replace project-specific design systems or accessibility review.
Assumes React, Tailwind CSS, and component primitive guidance are relevant.
Provides rules and review criteria, not a full product design system.

use_cases.title: Review UI Before Release
use_cases.description: Find accessibility, animation, typography, and layout issues before a frontend change ships.

use_cases.title: Standardize AI-Generated Components
use_cases.description: Apply consistent rules when AI creates or edits React and Tailwind CSS components.

use_cases.title: Guide Product Surface Refactors
use_cases.description: Keep dashboards, forms, and interaction surfaces aligned with practical UI quality rules.

prompt_templates.title: Apply The Baseline
prompt_templates.prompt: Use baseline-ui for this feature. Keep the interface accessible, responsive, and consistent with existing components.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a new UI task

prompt_templates.title: Review A Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the attached component with baseline-ui. List violations, why each matters, and a concrete fix.
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused review of one file or component

prompt_templates.title: Audit Interaction Details
prompt_templates.prompt: Use baseline-ui to review this interaction design. Focus on animation properties, reduced motion, timing, and performance risks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review for motion and interaction quality

prompt_templates.title: Refactor A Complex Surface
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply baseline-ui to this dashboard redesign. Preserve existing primitives, reduce visual noise, and call out important tradeoffs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review for a dense product interface

output_examples.input: Review a destructive confirmation modal before release.
output: Violation: the destructive action uses a generic dialog instead of an alert dialog.
Why it matters: keyboard and focus behavior must match the risk of the action.
Fix: use the project alert dialog primitive and keep the destructive action explicit.

output_examples.input: Apply the baseline to a metrics dashboard design.
output: Recommendation: use tabular numbers for metric values and dense tables.
Recommendation: use structural loading states near the affected data region.
Recommendation: keep square controls on stable size utilities to avoid layout shifts.

output_examples.input: Check animation choices for a panel transition.
output: Violation: the transition animates layout dimensions instead of compositor properties.
Why it matters: layout animation can cause poor performance and visual instability.
Fix: animate transform and opacity, keep feedback under 200 milliseconds, and respect reduced motion.

best_practices: Apply the skill before final UI implementation, then review again before release.
Use the project existing primitives and theme tokens before adding new UI patterns.
Pair the review with rendered screenshots and accessibility checks for important flows.
anti_patterns: Using the skill to override a mature project design system without review.
Treating the checklist as a substitute for keyboard, screen reader, or visual testing.
Applying React and Tailwind CSS guidance to unrelated stacks without adapting it.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews frontend UI decisions across stack choices, components, interaction, animation, typography, layout, performance, and visual design.

faq.question: Does it generate production code?
faq.answer: It mainly provides constraints and review guidance. It can guide code changes when used with an implementation task.

faq.question: Which stacks fit best?
faq.answer: It fits React and Tailwind CSS projects that use accessible component primitives and modern animation libraries.

faq.question: Can it replace accessibility testing?
faq.answer: No. It improves accessibility habits, but teams should still test keyboard flow, focus behavior, and assistive technology support.

faq.question: How should teams use it?
faq.answer: Use it as a shared baseline during AI-assisted design, implementation, and review of frontend surfaces.

faq.question: Does it require external services?
faq.answer: No. The skill is a Markdown instruction file and does not call external services.
